subject: cosmonaut in space station
title: What If Your Country Vanished While You Were in Orbit? It Happened in 1991

scenes.text: What if your country disappeared while you were in space? One cosmonaut found out.
May 18, 1991. Sergei Krikalev lifts off from Baikonur, in Soviet Kazakhstan, bound for the Mir station.
Below him the Soviet Union is breaking apart. To keep the Kazakh launch site, Moscow gives his replacement's seat to a Kazakh. He stays up.
December 26, 1991. The Soviet Union ceases to exist. He is still circling Earth 16 times a day, paid a few dollars a month.
March 25, 1992. After 312 days and about 5,000 orbits, he lands in Kazakhstan, now a foreign country. Four men lift him out.
His hometown, Leningrad, is now St. Petersburg. His flag is gone. He went up a Soviet citizen and came down the last one.

description:
What if your country collapsed while you were in orbit? Cosmonaut Sergei Krikalev launched to Mir from Baikonur on 18 May 1991; while he circled Earth, Moscow gave the next seat to a Kazakh cosmonaut to keep the launch site, and the Soviet Union dissolved on 26 December 1991.
He landed on 25 March 1992 after 312 days and about 5,000 orbits, near Arkalyk in a newly independent Kazakhstan, with his hometown Leningrad renamed St. Petersburg.

first_comment: Krikalev later flew on the US Space Shuttle and the ISS, reaching 803 days in orbit. Which stranded-in-space story should we run through next?
